normalized.governing_thought: Onsoo should enter the US in 2027 with an Amazon-led launch: it is the only route that fits the board's financial rules, but it needs gates because payback depends on ad cost
executive_summary: 1 Enter the US in 2027, rather than scale up Japan
US K-beauty skincare is $3.6B, growing 17% a year (category: 5%), and 41% of it sells on Amazon.
The pilot shows demand: 64,800 units in six months at 4.5 stars, a $4.0M annualised run-rate, and 29% repeat (benchmark 31%).
Amazon-led gives $26.4M of US revenue in 2030 vs $7.0M of extra revenue from the Japan scale-up, with peak cash of only $1.9–3.2M.
2 Lead with Amazon, not a 600-door specialty-retail launch
Amazon-led passes all three financial tests: peak cash –$1.9M (cap $18M), payback in 2030, group margin never below 9.5%.
Retail-led fails all three on its own numbers: peak cash –$20.8M, no payback by 2030, group margin 4.5% in 2027.
Its key inputs do not hold: at Onsoo's 4% awareness, newcomers sell a median 2.6 units/door/week (plan: 4.5; delisting below 4.0), and the 1.3× halo rests on a correlation.
3 Launch with conditions, because three parts of the CEO's plan need changing
Payback holds only if ACoS ≤ 28.6%. At the 32% benchmark for brands this size, cash is still –$2.3M at end-2030, so set a 28% ACoS ceiling and hold a gate in March 2028.
Retail from 2029 at the planned cost would break payback and the margin floor. Enter retail after payback and above 20% awareness (not 15%).
No modeled route reaches $40M by 2030 inside the cash cap and payback rule. Keep the rules and move the $40M date to about 2032.
Decision for March 2027: approve the Amazon-led launch with a $4M cash envelope, a 28% ACoS ceiling and a gate in March 2028; defer specialty retail; move the $40M ambition to about 2032.

slides.title: We tested the CEO's starting hypothesis against seven conditions: the Amazon-first route holds, but payback, retail timing and the $40M date need changing

claims.claim: Product: Onsoo's products win with US Amazon shoppers — ✓ Holds, after a label fix
evidence: 4.5 stars from 2,140 reviews; units +89% Jan→Jun; repeat 29% vs 31% benchmark; 6% complain of Korean-only labels

claims.claim: Use of 2027: The US is a better use of the single 2027 launch slot than Japan — ✓ Holds
evidence: 2030 revenue $26.4M (US) vs $7.0M (Japan); both inside the constraints on plan; Japan grows 1.5%/yr

claims.claim: Route: Starting on Amazon beats starting in 600 specialty doors — ✓ Holds

claims.claim: Economics: Amazon-led meets the cash cap, payback and margin floor — ◐ Partly: payback at risk

evidence: Starting hypothesis (CEO): "Launch in the US in 2027 through Amazon, then add specialty beauty retail from 2029 once Amazon sales pass $10M and aided awareness passes 15%."

customer survey Sept 2026 (n=1,200 US women 18–44)

So what: the market is big enough, growing fast, and Amazon-centric. That favours an Amazon-led entry.

$4.0M annualised run-rate (June: 14,000 units × 12 × $24)

slides.title: An Amazon-led US launch is a better use of the single 2027 launch slot than the Japan scale-up: about four times the 2030 revenue for a small, capped downside

claims.claim: Comparison of A (plan / benchmark ACoS) vs J
evidence: Revenue in 2030: $26.4M | $26.4M | $7.0M (incremental)
Peak cumulative cash need, 2027–30: –$1.9M | –$3.2M | –$1.05M
Cumulative cash at end-2030: +$2.4M | –$2.3M | +$1.8M
Cash flow in 2030 (run-rate): +$2.7M | +$0.9M | +$1.3M
Lowest group operating margin, 2027–30: 9.5% | 9.1% | 10.1%
Board tests met (cap / payback / margin): ✓/✓/✓ | ✓/✗/✓ | ✓/✓/✓
Market growth: +17%/yr K-beauty; new market | +1.5%/yr; already 3.1% share
Worst case tested: Sales stall: –$7.1M by 2030, or about –$3M if stopped at the March 2028 gate | Japan: Small; not modeled in the pack

claims.claim: Scale: the US adds about 4× the revenue Japan does by 2030, and is still growing 29% a year in 2030.
Bounded downside: even the worst US case tested (–$7.1M) uses under 40% of the $18M cap.
Timing: the pilot has momentum and 2,140 reviews. Waiting a year cedes a market growing 17% a year.
Japan is the safer bet for 2030 cash (+$1.8M vs –$2.3M at benchmark ACoS). We give that up for the only option that moves the US ambition forward.
The bandwidth limit covers 2027 only, so we recommend looking at the Japan scale-up again for 2028.
So what: use 2027 for the US. Japan's extra cash does not make up for losing a year in a market growing 17% a year, and the US downside is small.

slides.title: Per unit, retail earns more than Amazon ($7.55 vs $4.73), but the retail route adds $7.5M a year of fixed cost that its unit margin cannot cover

claims.claim: Per-unit economics Amazon vs specialty retail
evidence: Price Onsoo receives: 24.00 | 14.00 (50% of $28 shelf)
Amazon referral fee (15%): –3.60 | —
Amazon FBA fee: –5.10 | —
Ex-factory product cost: –3.50 | –3.50
Import duty (15% of ex-factory): –0.53 | –0.53
Co-op marketing (8%) + returns (4%) of wholesale: — | –1.68
Contribution before advertising: 10.73 | 7.55
Advertising at 25% ACoS (plan) / 32% (benchmark): –6.00 / –7.68 | in fixed budget
Contribution per unit: 4.73 / 3.05 | 7.55

claims.claim: Retail's own break-even, at the planned cost base
evidence: Retail-only fixed cost: $6.0M national marketing + $1.5M field team = $7.5M a year.
Units needed = $7.5M ÷ $7.545 = 994k a year. Across 600 doors that is ÷ (600 × 52) = 32 units/door/week.
The plan assumes 4.5; the evidence for Onsoo suggests 2.6. At 4.5, retail would need ≈4,248 doors to cover its costs.
At 4.5 units/door/week, 600 doors sell 140k units: $2.0M of wholesale revenue against $7.5M of fixed cost.

claims.claim: Amazon's sensitivity is advertising
evidence: Each ACoS point costs $0.24 a unit, or ≈ $0.67M over the 2.81M units planned for 2027–30.
Unit break-even ACoS is 44.7%, but covering fixed costs by 2030 needs ≤ 28.6%

claims.claim: So what: retail only makes sense if it lifts Amazon sales enough to pay for itself. That rests on the halo assumption tested on page 10.

slides.title: Only the Amazon-led route passes all three of the board's financial tests; retail-led fails all three even on the planning team's own assumptions

claims.claim: Board tests by option (A / B / J)
evidence: Group margin ≥ 8% every year: ✓ low 9.5% | ✗ 4.5% in 2027 | ✓ low 10.1%
Ambition: 2030 revenue vs $40M: $26.4M | $37.6M | No US; +$7.0M Japan

evidence: Board cap: –$18M peak cash

B's cash is still falling in 2030 (–$1.9M that year), so it has no route to payback on the planning team's own inputs.

slides.title: Retail-led's 4.5 units/door/week comes from successful brands; at Onsoo's 4% awareness, newcomers sell a median 2.6, and most fall below the delisting bar

claims.claim: Median first-year units/door/week by awareness among category buyers
evidence: Below 10% (Onsoo today: 4%): 2.6, IQR 1.9–3.4
Option B assumes 4.5
Delisting bar: below 4.0 at the 12-month review
Table 8 (retail analytics firm, 2025, 46 newcomer brands)

claims.claim: Onsoo's aided awareness is 4% of category buyers (9% among K-beauty buyers), so it falls in the below-10% band.
In that band even the top quartile (3.4) is below the 4.0 bar. More than 75% of comparable newcomers would be removed at the 12-month review.
The 4.5 comes from the retailer's deck on successful newcomers, which is survivorship bias. It matches the above-20% band (4.6), five times Onsoo's awareness.
Mooncrest (retail-first, 450 doors, 2023) was removed from shelves in 2025 after an estimated $21M US loss.
With 2.6 units/door/week and no halo, retail-led's cumulative cash reaches –$26.4M by 2030.
So what: on the evidence, a 2027 national retail launch would probably be delisted in 2028, repeating Mooncrest's loss.

slides.title: The 1.3× Amazon "halo" behind retail-led rests on a correlation; to pay for retail's costs the halo would need to be 2.1–3.4× from 2028

claims.claim: Why a 0.71 correlation does not show that retail drives Amazon
evidence: Reverse causation: retailers sign brands that already sell. Saebom reached ~$30M on Amazon first and then added 300 doors in 2025.
Common cause: older, bigger, better-funded brands have both more doors and more Amazon sales.
Survivorship: the sample is 30 brands sold in the US today. Failures such as Mooncrest are probably not in it.
Size of effect: r = 0.71 means r² ≈ 0.50 shared variance. It says nothing about direction or about how big a 1.3× uplift would be.

claims.claim: Customer evidence points the other way
evidence: only 17% of K-beauty buyers found their last new brand in a store (38% on TikTok), and 22% buy at specialty retail most often

claims.claim: Amazon multiple needed for retail to cover its own costs
evidence: the 1.3× halo assumed in Option B (a 30% uplift)

claims.claim: So what: the halo may exist, but it is unproven. To pay for retail it would have to lift Amazon sales by 110–240%, not 30%. Measure it before paying $7.5M a year for it.

slides.title: Payback by 2030 is the binding constraint: Amazon-led pays back only if ACoS stays at or below 28.6%, while the benchmark for brands this size is 32%

claims.claim: Option A cumulative cash at end-2030 by ACoS
Cumulative cash at end-2030: ACoS × volume

The plan assumes ACoS falls to 25% as the brand matures. The agency data says it rises as brands bid on broader keywords, to a median of 32% between $5M and $20M a year, which is exactly A's path ($7.2M → $26.4M).
evidence: §11 (agency benchmark: median 32%, range 26–38% for brands scaling $5M→$20M on Amazon US)

claims.claim: At the pilot's 28%, volume must reach ≥ 96% of plan to pay back. At 25%, ≥ 79%.
The cash cap is never the issue: peak cash stays between –$1.9M and –$6.4M across 25–38% ACoS.
So what: treat ACoS as the key operating metric. Cap blended ACoS at 28%, and give up growth rather than buy volume above the ceiling. Re-forecast at 32% before launch.

slides.title: The downside is bounded: even if sales stall or tariffs rise, Amazon-led needs at most $7.1M of peak cash, well under the $18M cap, and group margin stays above the 8% floor

claims.claim: If sales stall and we stop at the March 2028 gate, the loss is about $3M (2027: –$2.6M, plus one quarter of 2028).
A 10% weaker won (≈ –$0.40 a unit) would roughly offset the tariff rise (+$0.35 a unit).
So what: the cash cap and margin floor are safe in every Amazon-led case. The real risk is payback. A gate can limit the cost of a stall to about $3M.

slides.title: Specialty retail should follow payback, not come before it: 600 doors in 2029 would break payback and the margin floor, and a 15% awareness gate is too low

claims.claim: Cumulative US cash, $M: A only vs A + 600 retail doors from 2029
Gates for entering retail: CEO's proposal vs recommended
evidence: Timing: From 2029 | Decide in 2030 for 2031 | 2029 entry: –$11.8M at 2030, margin 6.3%
Aided awareness: > 15% | > 20% | 10–20%: median 3.5 < 4.0 bar; >20%: median 4.6
Amazon sales: > $10M | > $10M (kept) | Reached in 2028 on plan; not binding
US cash: — | Cumulative ≥ 0 (payback met) | Board's payback rule
Cost base: National, $7.5M/yr | Scaled to doors | Needs 32 units/door/week at 600 doors

claims.claim: Raising awareness from 4% to 20% (5×) is the main brand-building job for 2027–30. TikTok (38% of discovery) is the main lever, so weight the $0.7M off-Amazon budget towards it. Re-run the awareness survey every year.
So what: keep retail in the plan but make it the next step after payback, triggered by >20% awareness rather than by the calendar.

slides.title: No modeled route reaches $40M by 2030 within the $18M cap and 2030 payback; we recommend keeping the financial rules and moving the $40M date to about 2032

claims.claim: US revenue in 2030 by route, $M, and board tests met
evidence: A · Amazon-led: 26.4 (✓ cap · ✓ payback / ✓ margin floor)
A + retail 2029: 28.4093 (✓ cap · ✗ payback / ✗ margin floor)
B · plan inputs: 37.596 (✗ cap · ✗ payback / ✗ margin floor)
B · evidence inputs: 28.2928 (✗ cap · ✗ payback / ✗ margin floor)
Ambition: $40M in 2030

claims.claim: Recommended: keep the rules, move the date. Read "on the way to $40M" as $25M+ in 2030 with a credible path to $40M around 2032.
evidence: A, continuing at ~25%/yr (illustrative): $26.4M (2030), $33.0M (2031), $41.3M (2032)
+ retail from 2031 if gates are met: upside

claims.claim: Not recommended: keep 2030, relax the rules. Only retail-led gets near $40M, and it needs a cap above $20.8M on optimistic inputs (–$26.4M on evidence inputs), no payback by 2030, and margins below 8% for three years.
So what: the $40M-by-2030 ambition cannot be met together with the board's $18M cap and 2030 payback rule. The board should formally choose which one gives way. We recommend the date.

slides.title: We recommend a three-phase plan in which each phase is unlocked by measured results rather than by the calendar

claims.claim: Phase 1 · Launch, Apr–Dec 2027
evidence: Set up the US entity, MoCRA registration and US-compliant labels (removes the Korean-only label complaint)
Move the listings from the cross-border seller to Onsoo's own Amazon operation
Add four SKUs (seven in total); weight the $0.7M off-Amazon budget to TikTok and social
Run at a blended ACoS ceiling of 28%; cash envelope $4M (covers the –$3.9M stress case)

claims.claim: Phase 2 · Scale on Amazon, 2028–2030
evidence: Scale towards ~1.1M units ($26M) only while ACoS ≤ 28%
Build aided awareness from 4% towards 20%; survey every year
Lift 90-day repeat from 29% to ≥ 31% through the wider range
Look again at the Japan scale-up for 2028 (bandwidth now free)

claims.claim: Phase 3 · Add retail, Decide 2030 → launch 2031
evidence: Only when awareness > 20% and US cash has paid back
Start with a door-scaled cost base, not the $7.5M national model
Measure the Amazon halo directly before scaling doors
Path to $40M around 2032

claims.claim: Gate 1 · March 2028 board on full-year 2027 results
evidence: Green: scale — ACoS ≤ 28% and units ≥ 96% of plan (re-forecast pays back by 2030); repeat ≥ 31%
Amber: hold — Anything between green and red: hold ad spend at the ceiling, slow SKU additions, re-forecast in 6 months
Red: stop — ACoS > 32% or units < 70% of plan (stall zone): move to a maintenance model or exit; cash at risk about $3M

claims.claim: KPIs tracked monthly
evidence: Blended ACoS: 28% (pilot) → ≤ 28% ceiling
Amazon units vs plan: 168k/yr run-rate → 300k in 2027 → 1.1M in 2030
90-day repeat: 29% → ≥ 31% by Gate 1

Cumulative US cash: — → ≥ –$4M envelope; ≥ 0 by 2030

slides.title: Appendix: interpretation choices and key modeling assumptions

claims.claim: Choices made where we would have asked
evidence: "$40M by 2030" is read as a 2030 revenue target and treated as an ambition. The cash cap, payback and margin floor are treated as hard constraints.
US revenue = what Onsoo receives: $24 on Amazon and $14 wholesale for retail, not shelf value.
Retail volumes run for the full year from 2027, as the planning team implies; no ramp-up.
Tariff stress applies 25% duty to all four years (conservative, since the decision is mid-2027).
Listings move from the cross-border seller to Onsoo's own operation inside the $0.8M setup cost.
Stall case = Amazon flat at 200k units ($4.8M) a year, consistent with peers below $5M.
Cash envelope $4M is our proposal, covering the worst non-stall stress case (–$3.9M).

claims.claim: Modeling conventions
evidence: Pre-tax US cash flow; constant FX (KRW 1,380/$); no terminal value.
Cash = units × unit contribution – fixed costs – one-time costs – change in inventory.
Inventory = 4 months of landed cost (ex-factory + freight + duty): $4.575 a unit on Amazon, $4.775 in retail.
Door fixtures ($1,100 per new door) expensed in the year the door opens.
Group margin = (ex-US plan revenue × 11% + US operating result) ÷ (ex-US revenue + US revenue). Inventory is excluded from the margin.
Hero-SKU unit economics applied to all SKUs, as the planning team does.
Japan (Option J): incremental revenue × 30% – $0.8M fixed – $1.0M one-time; no working-capital data provided.
Peak cash = the most negative cumulative cash position, 2027–30.
All inputs come from the briefing pack; no outside data used. Figures are synthetic benchmark data.

slides.title: Appendix: Option J (Japan scale-up) is low-risk and pays back in 2029, but adds only $7M of revenue by 2030

claims.claim: Option J · incremental revenue × 30% contribution; $0.8M fixed a year; $1.0M one-time in 2027
Key calculations used in the deck
evidence: Amazon contribution = 24.00 – 3.60 referral – 5.10 FBA – 3.50 product – 0.55 freight – 0.525 duty = $10.725 before ads; – 25% × $24 = $4.725.
Retail contribution = 14.00 – 3.50 – 0.75 – 0.525 – 1.12 co-op – 0.56 returns = $7.545; break-even at 600 doors = 7.5M ÷ 7.545 ÷ 31,200 = 31.9 units/door/week.
Break-even ACoS for 2030 payback: cumulative contribution must cover $9.2M of fixed and setup costs plus $1.68M of end-2030 inventory over 2.81M units → $3.87 a unit → ACoS ≤ 28.6%.
Tariff at 25%: duty $0.875 vs $0.525 → +$0.35 a unit × 2.81M = –$0.98M, plus –$0.13M of extra inventory = –$1.1M.
Pilot run-rate: 14,000 × 12 = 168k units = $4.03M; 2027 plan of 300k = 1.79× that.
group context (ex-US revenue $140M/$146M/$152M/$158M at 11.0% operating margin)

normalized.recommendation: Approve the Amazon-led launch (Option A) in 2027 with a $4M cash envelope, a 28% ACoS ceiling and a gate in March 2028; defer specialty retail (do not launch national specialty retail in 2027; revisit in 2030 for 2031, once awareness is above 20% and US cash has paid back); move the ambition to $25M+ US revenue in 2030 and $40M around 2032, keeping the cash cap, payback rule and margin floor unchanged; look again at the Japan scale-up for 2028.

alternatives_considered.treatment: Chosen. Passes all three financial tests: peak cash –$1.9M (cap $18M), payback in 2030, group margin never below 9.5%; $26.4M 2030 revenue. Payback only if ACoS ≤ 28.6% (fails at 32% benchmark), hence gated.

Rejected. Fails all three tests on its own numbers: peak cash –$20.8M, no payback by 2030, group margin 4.5% in 2027; key inputs (4.5 units/door/week, 1.3× halo) do not hold; –$26.4M on evidence inputs.

Not chosen for 2027. Safer bet for 2030 cash (+$1.8M vs –$2.3M at benchmark ACoS), pays back in 2029, but adds only $7.0M of revenue in a market growing 1.5%/yr; recommended to look at again for 2028.

alternatives_considered.option: CEO's phase 2: A + 600 retail doors from 2029 at $10M Amazon sales and 15% awareness
alternatives_considered.treatment: Rejected. Would break payback and the margin floor (–$11.8M at 2030, margin 6.3%); 15% awareness gate too low (10–20% band median 3.5 < 4.0 delisting bar). Replaced by: decide in 2030 for 2031, >20% awareness, payback met, door-scaled cost base.

alternatives_considered.option: Keep 2030 for the $40M ambition and relax the financial rules
alternatives_considered.treatment: Not recommended. Only retail-led gets near $40M, and it needs a cap above $20.8M on optimistic inputs (–$26.4M on evidence inputs), no payback by 2030, and margins below 8% for three years.

alternatives_considered.option: Keep the financial rules and move the $40M date to about 2032
alternatives_considered.treatment: Recommended. Read "on the way to $40M" as $25M+ in 2030 with a credible path to $40M around 2032.
Rejected: includes makeup and hair care; overstates Onsoo's addressable market by about 45%. Use $3.6B.

assumptions_and_uncertainties: "$40M by 2030" is read as a 2030 revenue target and treated as an ambition. The cash cap, payback and margin floor are treated as hard constraints.
US revenue = what Onsoo receives: $24 on Amazon and $14 wholesale for retail, not shelf value.
Retail volumes run for the full year from 2027, as the planning team implies; no ramp-up.
Tariff stress applies 25% duty to all four years (conservative, since the decision is mid-2027).
Listings move from the cross-border seller to Onsoo's own operation inside the $0.8M setup cost.
Stall case = Amazon flat at 200k units ($4.8M) a year, consistent with peers below $5M.
Cash envelope $4M is our proposal, covering the worst non-stall stress case (–$3.9M).
Pre-tax US cash flow; constant FX (KRW 1,380/$); no terminal value.
Hero-SKU unit economics applied to all SKUs, as the planning team does.
Japan: incremental figures as given (no working-capital data provided); Japan worst case not modeled in the pack.
All inputs come from the briefing pack; no outside data used. Figures are synthetic benchmark data.
Post-2030 path is illustrative: assumes ~25% a year growth after 2030 (A grew 29% in 2030); not in the planning data.
Payback holds only if ACoS ≤ 28.6%; benchmark for brands this size is 32% (range 26–38%).
The Amazon halo may exist, but it is unproven.
Risk: Ad cost at scale – –$0.67M per ACoS point; 32% → –$2.3M (no payback).
Risk: Demand stall – 2 of 3 Amazon-first peers stayed below $5M; –$7.1M by 2030 if continued; about –$3M if stopped at Gate 1.
Risk: Tariff 15% → 25% – +$0.35/unit; –$1.1M; break-even ACoS 28.6% → 26.9%; decision mid-2027.
Risk: Low repeat – 29% vs 31% benchmark; lower lifetime value means more reliance on ads.
Risk: FX (KRW/USD) – 10% weaker won = +$0.40/unit (upside); stronger won is the mirror risk.
Risk: Launch execution – Korean-only labels in 6% of reviews; first US entity; MoCRA compliance.
2027 plan needs 300k units = 1.8× the June run-rate; from today's 3 SKUs alone that takes ~4.6% monthly growth through 2027.
